lane: email

# Fortress 1.2.9: what's new

- Work computer and phone privacy: a short checklist for anyone with a work laptop or work phone. Keep personal browsing, messages, banking and shopping off work devices and work Wi-Fi; don't plug your own phone into a work computer or tap "Trust This Computer"; ask IT what a work profile can see before you put one on your own phone; use mobile data on work Wi-Fi; close or cover the webcam when you're not on a call.
- Is this computer managed by my employer? Fortress shows where to look on a Mac (Device Management) and on Windows (Access work or school), with Apple's and Microsoft's own help pages, checked on 17 Nov 2026. Look only: don't remove company software.
- Said plainly: a work device belongs to your employer. Fortress can't see or remove monitoring software, and rules on workplace monitoring differ by state and country. Some employers buy background reports, so the people-search opt-outs and social account lockdown help here too.
- This checklist is in English only for now. It isn't in Japanese yet.
- If you're coming from 1.2.7, this update also brings everything from 1.2.8:
  - Lockdown phrase: pick a phrase (or just say "Fortress lockdown"). If someone's got into your account, someone's following or exposing you online, or your phone's lost, Fortress walks you through one step at a time in a set order: your safety, your phone, your email, your mobile network, your bank, your social accounts, location sharing, then a dated record. Every step opens the company's own help page; you tap, Fortress never logs in for you.
  - If the police, a court or a solicitor is involved, Fortress won't delete, hide or clean up anything (X Post Cleaner included). It sticks to passwords, sign-ins and locks, and shows the official GOV.UK and Law Society pages for finding a solicitor. It doesn't give legal advice.
  - Before you turn off location sharing, Fortress reminds you that if someone's watching it, they may notice it stop. If you're in danger, call 999. You decide.
  - UK scam cards: "move your money to a safe account", couriers collecting cash or cards, fake bank fraud teams, fake FCA or police, investment and crypto pitches (Fortress checks the FCA Register), "we'll get your money back" firms, HMRC, DWP, DVLA, TV Licensing, council-tax and energy rebate texts, pension offers, doorstep traders (Fortress drafts the 14-day cancel letter; you sign and send it), tickets and holidays, and romance scams. Any "bank" call: hang up and ring 159 from another phone.
  - Money back, said plainly: since 7 Oct 2024 UK rules cover bank-transfer scams sent by Faster Payments, up to £85,000, but your bank decides whether your case qualifies. Card, cash and crypto go other ways. Fortress never promises a refund; if the bank says no, it points you to the Financial Ombudsman.
  - No credit freeze in the UK: Fortress helps you get your free credit reports from Experian, Equifax and TransUnion and fix mistakes, and mentions Cifas Protective Registration (paid) only if you ask. Home: HM Land Registry's free Property Alert (England and Wales) tells you if someone tries to change your title.
  - Also for the UK: mobile network account protection (not every network has an extra PIN), what an unexpected PAC or STAC text means, a social account-security pack for 14 apps, a quiet-at-home checklist (TPS, MPS, open register), help for older relatives (Banking Protocol, trusted contacts, LPA on GOV.UK only) and gambling blocks if you ask for them. Fortress never asks for your National Insurance number or date of birth, and it never fills in an LPA.
  - Every company help page Fortress links in this update was checked on 16 Nov 2026. If a page has moved by the time you use it, Fortress gives you the menu path instead of guessing a link.
  - If you're coming from 1.2.6, this update also brings everything from 1.2.7:
    - Charge finder: download a card or bank statement (PDF or CSV) and drop it in the chat. Fortress lists the charges that come back every month and flags small charges under $5 and repeating ones it can't match to a company you know. You decide what each one is.
    - Cancel help: Fortress opens the company's own cancel page (24 US services checked so far; Hulu, Disney+ and Xbox Game Pass come later) and does the clicks with you. It stops at every offer to stay and before the final button, and it only calls something cancelled when the company's page or email says so. Adobe's yearly plan paid monthly can cost an early-cancel fee (half of what's left on the year after the first 14 days); Fortress shows the fee before you decide.
    - "I didn't sign up for this": Fortress writes what to tell your card company (tell them within 60 days of the statement) and how to ask for a new card number, and fills in an FTC report that waits for your OK. It can't dispute a charge for you or promise money back.
    - Your privacy: Fortress never connects to your bank. It hides card and account numbers down to the last 4 as soon as it reads the file, deletes its copy when you're done and doesn't save a separate copy unless you save the summary. If Gmail is already connected, it can also read receipt emails (read only). It can't read photos of paper statements or extra charges on phone bills yet. There's no federal click-to-cancel rule in effect right now: a court threw out the FTC's 2024 rule in July 2025.
    - Japan: Japanese card and bank statements can be read too (beta), and general cancel help on the official page works too. Japan-specific cancel steps and card-company steps come in the next update.
    - If you're coming from 1.2.5, this update also brings everything from 1.2.6:
      - Photo-access checkup: Fortress helps you see which apps can open your whole photo library and cut that back to none or only the photos you pick, on Android (Settings → Apps → the app → Permissions → Photos and videos) and iPhone (Settings → Privacy & Security → Photos). On Facebook it also walks you to Camera roll sharing suggestions so you can switch them off. Every step links Google's, Apple's or Meta's own help page, and older relatives get a simple drawn path first.
      - Why now: on 14 Nov 2026 Italy's privacy regulator fined Meta €805 million over a Facebook for Android feature that read the photo gallery through one app-wide permission and was on by default. Meta says it will appeal. Using photos to train AI wasn't part of the case, and Meta denies it.
      - Fortress can't change your phone settings itself. It opens the right help page, goes one step at a time and checks back with you. If a menu name on your screen is different, it goes by your screen. Meta's help page doesn't name every camera-roll switch yet, so Fortress asks what you see instead of guessing.
      - Privacy watch: when Fortress runs its weekly privacy check for you, it now also reads official announcements from the privacy regulators of Italy, France, Ireland and the EU. If one of them fines or orders a company whose app you use, Fortress tells you what was decided, whether it affects you and which setting to check. A fine that's being appealed isn't final, and Fortress never promises anyone a payout.
    - If you're coming from 1.2.4 or earlier, this update also brings everything from 1.2.5:
      - Japan: Fortress can now guide you in Japanese. The Japanese text is a beta: a native speaker hasn't finished checking it yet, so confirm official names, deadlines and fees on the official page Fortress links.
      - Japan, for older relatives and caregivers: Japanese safety cards for the most common scams (ATM "tax refund" calls, someone coming to collect your bank card, オレオレ family-emergency calls with a safe word, fake police), simple-Japanese wording, and a Japanese caregiver summary that's only sent after the person says yes.
      - Japan: official sender domains for 13 more brands that scammers imitate (楽天市場, 楽天カード, 楽天モバイル, 三井住友カード, JCB, セゾン, 三菱UFJ銀行, 三井住友銀行, みずほ銀行, docomo, au, SoftBank, PayPay), each taken from the company's own page. A matching domain is a clue, not proof, so Fortress still sends you to the official app to check. au doesn't publish a full list, so its entry is partial.
      - Japan: more checks and report routes: SNS investment and romance scam signs with the FSA's 0570-050588 line, Rakuten Mobile's spam SMS form, SoftBank's SMS report address, SAGICHECK for shopping sites (it says itself its results aren't perfect), and fake missed-delivery texts using Yamato, Sagawa or Japan Post.
      - Japan: when Fortress runs its weekday fraud watch for you, it only marks something Confirmed from official Japanese pages (NPA, 国民生活センター, 消費者庁, the Anti-Phishing Council, JC3, NTA, FSA).
      - What Fortress can't do in Japan, said plainly in Japanese: Japan has no national Do Not Call list, no per-call damages and no credit freeze (only the paid 本人申告 note). Fortress can't call Japanese numbers or block calls on your phone. You make the calls and change the settings, with step-by-step help.
      - US banking scams: new cards for fake bank regulators (FDIC, OCC, Federal Reserve, CFPB), "move your money to protect it", gold or cash couriers, "send the money to yourself" Zelle calls, fake fraud alerts, washed checks and forged deeds. Fortress does the work where it can: it fills in the FTC, FBI (IC3), FDIC, CFPB and Postal Inspection reports, writes the bank call script and, where Fortress can place calls, makes the call to your bank with you. It always asks you first, every time, before anything is sent, submitted or dialed. Older relatives get one short step at a time.
      - Bank refunds, said correctly: if someone else moved your money (even with a code they tricked out of you), tell your bank it was unauthorized; federal rules (Reg E) cover that, and reporting fast limits what you can lose. If you sent it yourself after being lied to, it usually isn't, and wires aren't; ask anyway, but Fortress never promises money back.
      - Forged deeds: Fortress looks for your county's free recording alert on the county's own site and fills in the sign-up; you type anything private. The alert tells you after something is filed; it doesn't block it. If Fortress can't tell, it says to check with your county clerk.
      - Japan: gold handed to fake police, people pretending to be from 金融庁, 日本銀行, 預金保険機構 or 銀行協会, online-banking theft, and title fraud (不正登記防止申出). Fortress writes your #9110 and 188 call notes; you make the calls.
      - US scams that cost people the most: investment pitches (Fortress looks the person or firm up on FINRA BrokerCheck, the SEC adviser database and your state securities regulator), "we'll get your money back" offers, task and job scams, fake jury-duty, warrant, Social Security, IRS and Medicare calls (with the right office to report each one to), "you won, just pay the fee" letters, and door-to-door "free inspection" repairs (Fortress fills in the cancellation letter; you sign and mail it).
      - Unclaimed money: Fortress searches MissingMoney.com and the official site of each state you've lived in, and can check old pensions, lost savings bonds and money from failed banks. Searching and claiming are free. Fortress fills in a claim only after you say yes, and you type anything private on the official site yourself.
      - Japan: side-job scams, "we'll get your money back" second scams, door-to-door inspection sales (Fortress drafts the cooling-off postcard), scam scouting calls, a new fake-police video-call trick, and how to get a dormant bank account (休眠預金) back at your bank.
- It always asks you first before anything is sent, submitted or claimed.
- If you're still on 1.2.2 or 1.2.3, this update also brings everything from 1.2.3 (the Japan pack (Japanese scam checks, carrier mail filter coaching and report drafts)) and 1.2.4 (TELUS Scam Protection in the Canada carrier list).
- Your setup stays as it was. This update doesn't touch your settings, safe list, opt-ins, labels, logs or caregiver choices, and it doesn't re-run setup.

Undo: say "undo the Fortress update" and I'll put your previous version back. If you updated straight from 1.2.2, that means back to 1.2.2.

## Fortress：新しくなったこと（日本向け・日本語ベータ版）

- 請求チェックを追加しました。カードや銀行の明細（PDF・CSV）を送ると、くり返しの請求と心当たりのない少額の請求を探し、解約はサービスの公式ページで一緒に手続きします。日本の各サービスに合わせた解約手順は、次の更新で追加します。銀行とはつなぎません（ベータ版）。
- 写真へのアクセスの点検を追加しました。どのアプリが写真フォルダ全体を見られるかを確かめ、Facebookのカメラロールの提案をオフにする手順を、公式ヘルプのリンク付きでご案内します。設定を変えるのはご本人です。
- 週1回のプライバシーチェックで、イタリア・フランス・アイルランド・EUの個人情報保護機関の公式発表も確認するようになりました。お使いのサービスについて制裁金や命令が出たときは、決定の内容、ご自身への影響、確認する設定をお知らせします。
- 日本：案内が日本語になりました（ベータ版。ネイティブスピーカーによる確認を反映しました）。
- 日本：ご高齢の方向けの「お守りカード」を追加しました（還付金・キャッシュカード・オレオレ・ニセ警察）。見守りの方向けの日本語のまとめも作れます。
- 日本：楽天・カード会社（三井住友カード・JCB・セゾン・楽天カード）・3メガバンク・携帯会社（ドコモ・au・ソフトバンク・楽天モバイル）・PayPayの公式ドメインを追加しました。なりすましメールを見分けやすくなります（ドメインが同じでも偽物のことがあります）。
- 日本：SNS型投資詐欺・ロマンス詐欺のチェックと、金融庁の相談窓口を追加しました。
- 日本：平日の詐欺情報チェックで、警察庁・国民生活センター・フィッシング対策協議会などの公式情報を確認します。
- 日本でできないこと（国の電話勧誘お断りリスト、迷惑電話1件ごとの損害賠償、信用情報の凍結、日本の番号への発信、端末での着信ブロック）も、日本語ではっきりお伝えします。
- 1.2.2・1.2.3からの方も、この更新で日本向けパック（1.2.3）とカナダのTELUS（1.2.4）がまとめて入ります。
- 日本：金（きん）を渡させるニセ警察、金融庁・日本銀行・預金保険機構・銀行協会を名乗る詐欺、ネットバンキングの不正送金、不正な不動産登記への備えを追加しました。#9110・188の相談メモはFortressが書きます。
- 日本：副業詐欺、「お金を取り戻す」という二次被害、点検商法（クーリング・オフのはがきの下書き）、予兆電話（アポ電）、ニセ警察の新しい手口、休眠預金の案内を追加しました。送る・申し込む前には、必ずご本人に確認します。
- これまでの設定はそのままです。設定・安全リスト・記録・見守りの選択は変わらず、設定のやり直しもありません。
- 元に戻すときは「Fortressの更新を元に戻して」と送ってください。更新前のバージョンに戻します（1.2.2から更新した場合は1.2.2に戻ります）。

# Phone Spam Fortress — Capability matrix (US states + international)

_Last updated 2026-10-27 (America/Los_Angeles). Not legal advice. Every "money" cell is a **possible claim path**, never money received. Sources: official pages loaded on 2026-10-27 plus tcpa.com state guides (secondary, labelled). Machine-readable data: `states/us-states.json`, `sites-international.json`._

## What "fullest capability" means
The bot works on three pillars, and how far each one goes depends on where the user lives:

1. **Block / suppress.** Do-not-call registries, carrier and phone tools, data-broker and directory opt-outs, and regulator spam reporting. This works everywhere and is always the first step.
2. **Letters / rights requests.** Opt-out and stop-calling letters, privacy-law requests (GDPR Art. 21/17/15, PIPEDA, LGPD, APPs), and regulator or AG complaints. This works in nearly every jurisdiction listed. Under 47 CFR 64.1200(d), US callers must also keep internal do-not-call lists.
3. **Money / private claims.** Only where a statute lets an individual sue: the US federal TCPA everywhere in the US, plus the "strong" states below. Outside the US there is almost never a per-call amount. Regulator fines go to the government, and privacy-law compensation (GDPR Art. 82, UK DPA s.168, AU privacy tort, BR consumer courts) requires proven harm. The bot only **drafts**. A demand letter needs the user's explicit approval before it is sent, and it must never use US TCPA damages for a non-US resident.

"Fullest capability" therefore means:
- run every free blocking path available to the user;
- send the strongest rights letter local law supports;
- surface a money path **only** where one is verified, with a statute citation and an honesty note.

## United States — federal layer (applies in all 50 states + DC + territories)
| Pillar | What applies |
|---|---|
| Block | [National Do Not Call Registry](https://www.donotcall.gov/), carrier tools (STIR/SHAKEN labels, carrier blocking apps), phone settings |
| Letters / complaints | [FCC complaint](https://consumercomplaints.fcc.gov/hc/en-us), [FTC ReportFraud](https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/), stop/opt-out letter, internal-DNC request |
| Money | [47 U.S.C. 227](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/47/227): $500/violation, up to $1,500 willful. 227(b) covers robocalls, prerecorded calls, and autodialers; 227(c)(5) covers more than one DNC call in 12 months. |
| Cautions | *Facebook v. Duguid* (2021) narrowed the autodialer definition. *McLaughlin v. McKesson* (2025) holds courts are not bound by FCC readings. *Steidinger v. Blackstone* (7th Cir., July 2026, per secondary source) holds texts are not "calls" for the 227(c)(5) DNC claim; binding in IL/IN/WI federal courts. |

**State status key:**
- **strong**: a state statute gives per-call or statutory damages without requiring a purchase.
- **limited**: requires a loss or purchase, or has a narrow scope.
- **none**: enforcement is by the AG or an agency only, so the money path is federal TCPA.
- **uncertain**: not yet researched.

Counts: strong 18, limited 22, none 10, uncertain 1 (DC).

**International honesty rules:**
- No US TCPA math or demand letters for non-US residents.
- Registries and rules differ by EU member state:
  - FR Bloctel ended 11 Aug 2026; France now uses a consent rule.
  - NL is opt-in.
  - DE uses a consent rule (UWG §7) with no state list; it has the industry DDV-Robinsonliste (free; only https://www.ichhabediewahl.de/, updated 2026-11-11).
- Russia is information only; the bot does not push complaints there.
- `limited_verify` means a court-based compensation route exists in principle, but harm must be proven and there is no fixed per-call amount. Suggest a local lawyer or consumer body.
